text:
Jaroslav Chmelar is rediscovering his game, per The Hockey News, and has two goals in his last ten games, both in early November, in Seattle and Edmonton. He's a 23-year-old fifth-round pick from Czechia playing about nine minutes a night on the Rangers' fourth line.

He got his biggest workload in weeks against Carolina on Nov 22, 11:24 on a line with Eeli Tolvanen and Noah Laba. With Oliver Bjorkstrand out for two to three months, there's room to move up.

The on-ice numbers aren't there yet. New York gets 42% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, almost 12 points worse than without him. The goals have come on 1.5 expected, about what his chances deserve.

NHL Edge has his top speed at the 87th percentile, and he's thrown 29 hits in 15 games. What to watch: whether he can hold a third-line spot. The Rangers need bodies, and he's in the right place at the right time.
